name: Nairobi Contemporary Art Institute
funding: Non-profit founded 2020 by artist Michael Armitage; no funder list on its site as of Oct 2026, only unnamed library donors.
watch: No funder roster is published. Programme partners include Triangle and KSB TURN2.
records_note: Its site posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; partners appear only inside event descriptions.

name: Nasher Sculpture Center
funding: No donor list is published. Its credit line names only TACA, the Texas Commission on the Arts, and unnamed members and donors. FY2025 revenue was $14.0M, nearly all contributions.
watch: Private collection gifted to the public in Dallas's arts district.
records_note: Seven trustees are named on its site and Form 990s from 2003 to 2025 are on ProPublica; no annual report or donor list was found.

name: National Art Gallery of The Bahamas
funding: Non-profit with a government subvention plus private donors, memberships and admissions.
records_note: It posts audited accounts for 2014 to 2024 and names its board, but no annual reports and no donor list.

name: National Asian Culture Center (ACC)
funding: Government agency of Korea's Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism that plans and spends its own budget; operations are shared with the ACC Foundation.
watch: State-funded. The only criticism found is governance (the two-part set-up), not sponsors.
records_note: Its site posts yearly introduction brochures and programme guides but no financial reports, funder list or board.

name: National Centre for Contemporary Arts
watch: State body formed 1 Oct 2015 by merging the Museum of Modern Fine Arts (1997) with the Creative Workshops centre; c.4,936 works; venues at Nekrasova 3 and Independence Ave 47. Director Siarhei Kryshtapovich (since 2018) was commissioner of Belarus's last official Venice pavilion, 'Exit' (2019), organised with the Culture Ministry and the embassy in Italy.
records_note: A state-budget body being liquidated under a 3 August 2026 resolution; its site no longer resolves and the ministry posts no accounts for it.

name: National Gallery of Armenia
funding: A state gallery on Republic Square, founded in 1921 and run under Armenia's Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports; its budget and sponsors were not found.
watch: Armenia's largest art collection, about 42,000 works.
records_note: The gallery's site carries no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; it lists branches, collection, visits and education only.

name: National Gallery of Jamaica
watch: CHASE Fund and the Tourism Enhancement Fund are public funds. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: The gallery's own site refused connections, and its parent, the Institute of Jamaica, posts no annual reports, accounts or board list on its site.

name: National Gallery of Zimbabwe
funding: Parastatal under the Ministry of Youth, Sports, Arts and Recreation, plus unnamed sponsors.
records_note: Names its board of trustees but shows sponsor logos without names or dates; no annual reports or accounts found on the site.

name: National Museum, Lagos
funding: Federal Government through the National Commission for Museums and Monuments; IHS Nigeria, a telecom-tower company, funded a 2026 renovation. A Ford Foundation refit stalled.
watch: Reopened April 2026 after renovation. No NNPC, Shell, TotalEnergies or Dangote money found.
records_note: A federal museum with no records of its own; the parent commission's site posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or governing council.

name: National Museum of Damascus
funding: Its parent body, the Directorate-General of Antiquities and Museums, partners UNESCO's 2025 project: initial budget $175,000, no donor named. No museum budget is published.
watch: Closed 7 December 2024 after the fall of Damascus and reopened 8 January 2025. Wikipedia reports six Roman statues stolen in a November 2025 break-in.
records_note: The parent Directorate-General of Antiquities and Museums publishes no annual reports, accounts, donors or board; it is tied to the Minister of Culture.

name: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA)
funding: State museum. Hyundai Motor sponsored its series from 2014 to February 2024; LG Electronics sponsors the OLED Series from 2025. The Lee Kun-hee estate gave nearly 1,500 works in 2021.
watch: Hyundai Motor sponsored its series to February 2024. Reuters found children as young as 12 at Hyundai subsidiary SMART Alabama in 2022.
records_note: The state museum posts no annual report, accounts, sponsor list or board on its site; its sponsorship page points to a separate foundation site.

name: National Museum of Tajikistan
funding: No funder, budget or annual report found in the sources opened. Its official site did not load.
watch: Established 1934; renamed National Museum of Tajikistan in 2011 and moved into a new building in March 2013 with 22 halls and over 50,000 objects.
records_note: No museum site loaded; a government portal shows it is a state institution under the president's office, and no reports, accounts or funders appear.
